identity.note: GENERATION MATTERS AND WAS INITIALLY GOT WRONG. The van this file exists for is a 2024 E-Transit Custom, i.e. SECOND generation. Earlier proportion work in this session compared it against FIRST-generation figures (L 4973, W 1986, H 1925-2000) recalled from memory, which is exactly what the accuracy rule forbids. Those gen-1 numbers are real, they are simply the wrong car. Trim and model year are NOT asserted beyond what the source photo shows.

length_m.source: Parkers 2024-dimensions page AND Vansdirect load-sizing guide, independently, both 5050mm for L1 (L2 = 5450mm)

width_m.source: Parkers 2024-dimensions page, 2032mm EXCLUDING mirrors. SINGLE-SOURCED - flagged deliberately. Corroborated indirectly: Parkers and Vansdirect BOTH give 2275mm including mirrors, so this implies 243mm of total mirror overhang (~121mm per side), which is physically sensible for a van, and Parkers agrees with the other sources on every figure they share.

height_m.source: Parkers 1966-1968mm for H1; Vansdirect 1968mm. Midpoint of the Parkers range taken. H2 high roof is 2464-2471mm and is NOT this vehicle.

wheelbase_m.source: Parkers 3100mm for L1 (L2 = 3500mm); Wikipedia gives the generation range as 3100-3500mm, consistent

width_incl_mirrors_m.source: Parkers AND Vansdirect, independently. Recorded because fit_spec must NOT fit a Z extent to this figure - it is here so the mirror overhang can be reasoned about, not fitted to.

tyre.source: PROVISIONAL - a common OE fitment for this class, NOT verified for this specific van. Used only as an in-mesh absolute ruler to attribute a proportion error to an axis; the attribution was separately shown to be robust to this assumption (rescaling any single axis to correct still leaves width the outlier), so a wrong tyre size shifts the absolute metres but not the conclusion.

expect.note: No axle self-test values: this is a GENERATED body whose arches have not been aligned to spec, and pinning expected axle positions from an unaligned mesh would encode the error as ground truth.
